match.reason: No bank point teaches technological change alone as a planning question about how a market may look in a few years; the closest card, on technological, geographic and institutional influences, covers three influences at once, so it is broader than this point.

rejected.title: Technological change
card: Technological change means new tools, machines and software that alter what people can buy and how things are made or sold. A business cannot control it, but it must plan for it.
It can change the market. New products may replace old ones, and customers may come to expect new ways to order, pay or get help.
It can also change how a business works. Software, automation or online systems may cut costs or save time, but they can cost money to set up and staff may need training.
Planners look ahead and ask how the market may look in a few years. They then decide whether to adopt new technology, change their product or prepare for new rivals.
rejected.remember: Technology can change both the market and the way a business runs, so planners look ahead.

a.q: Why do planners of a new business ask how technology may change the market in a few years?
opts: Today's products and methods may be out of date by then
Technology always lowers a new business's costs
The business can decide how fast technology changes
Technology only affects how a business takes payments
a.why: Technology can change what customers want and how rivals operate, so a plan built only on today's market may fail. The idea that technology always cuts costs is wrong: it can also be costly to set up.
a.clue: Think about what the market may look like later.

b.q: Sam plans to open a shop in Ballarat that hires out DVDs. Streaming services keep growing. What is the best use of technological thinking in Sam's plan?
opts: Ask how customers may watch films in a few years
Wait to see whether customers stop visiting the shop
Lower the hire price to match the other local shops
Focus on shop layout, as technology is outside Sam's control
b.why: Planners look ahead to see how technology may change what customers want. Sam cannot control technology, but still has to plan for it. Saying it is outside Sam's control is tempting, but it is a reason to plan, not to ignore it.
b.clue: A business cannot control this factor, but it must still plan for it.
